title: Adaptive Momentum by Momentum for Deep Neural Network Training

problem.claim: Fixed momentum hyperparameters require extensive tuning and can prevent optimizers from achieving their best performance.

gap.claim: Standard momentum methods lack an adaptive mechanism that reduces momentum-tuning burden across optimization settings.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes an adaptive momentum mechanism motivated by optimal heavy-ball momentum for quadratic objectives.
The proposed mechanism is evaluated across image classification, language modeling, machine translation, tabular learning, and time-series classification benchmarks.
Convergence guarantees are established for SGD and Adam when used with the proposed adaptive momentum.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report improved stability for SGD and Adam under large learning rates.
The authors report faster convergence and better generalization than standard SGD and Adam in their experiments.
The authors report effectiveness across a wide range of machine learning benchmarks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Momentum accelerates gradient-based optimization in machine learning.
Fixed and one-size-fits-all momentum parameters create tuning burdens and may limit optimizer performance.
The paper proposes adaptive momentum motivated by optimal heavy-ball momentum for quadratic objectives.
The authors report improved stability, convergence, generalization, and benchmark effectiveness, and provide convergence guarantees for SGD and Adam.
